source.author: verg
source.text: Tuque ades inceptumque una decurre laborem, O decus, o famae merito pars maxima nostrae, Maecenas, pelagoque volans da vela patenti; non ego cuncta meis amplecti versibus opto, non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum, ferrea vox; ades et primi lege litoris oram.
source.text_original: Tuque ades inceptumque una decurre laborem, / O decus, o famae merito pars maxima nostrae, / Maecenas, pelagoque volans da vela patenti; / non ego cuncta meis amplecti versibus opto, / non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum, / ferrea vox; ades et primi lege litoris oram.
source.text_english: And you too be present and run through the task I have begun with me, O honor, O the greatest part of our fame deservedly ours, Maecenas, and fly forth with sails into the open sea; I do not hope to embrace everything in my verses, no, not if I had a hundred tongues and a hundred mouths, a voice of iron; be present, and pick the shore of the first coast.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum ferrea uox, omnes scelerum comprendere formas, omnia poenarum percurrere nomina possim, quae iudices per prouincias iustis atque innocentibus intulerunt.
reuse.text_original: non, mihi si linguae centum <sint> oraque centum ferrea uox, omnes scelerum comprendere formas, omnia poenarum percurrere nomina possim, quae iudices per prouincias iustis atque innocentibus intulerunt.
reuse.text_english: No, even if I had a hundred tongues, a hundred mouths, and a voice of iron, I could not recount all the kinds of crimes, or run through all the names of punishments, that the judges in the provinces inflicted on the just and innocent.
